name: skill-orchestrator
description: Tiered orchestration for screenplay production Skills: quick single-role advice, scoped role councils, and sealed, recoverable multi-Agent runs. Includes screenplay breakdown, scene direction, prompt compilation, and a capability registry for other installed plugins.

interface.shortDescription: Tiered screenplay direction: quick advice, role councils, and sealed multi-Agent runs.
interface.longDescription: An evidence-first screenplay and directing pipeline for Codex. The prompt-free scene director seals structured decisions, then a dedicated prose compiler renders one shot or subshot per Chinese paragraph in a table-free DOCX. Legacy XLSX materialization and the separate explicit Seedance compiler remain available without entering the default director workflow. Local v0.8.1 adds shared lighting/material enhancement and causal prompt translation; no NVIDIA rendering integration. Local v0.8.2 makes the Skill index pick each plugin's highest cached version and skip vendored copies; only the 12 index unit tests were run. User trial build; no sample, runtime, or effect tests executed. Local v0.9.0 adds three entry tiers (Light, Standard, Formal), layered capability registries that give other plugins' Skills domains and types, a code-enforced dynamic-expert gate, and a bundled native bridge that replaces per-run hand-written bridges. Index, registry, and bridge unit tests were run; no model-driven end-to-end run was executed.
capabilities: DLSS 5-style lighting and material enhancement planning
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $skill-orchestrator and state the tier you chose: Light for unsealed single-role advice, Standard for a scoped role council, Formal for a sealed run. Use $ai-script-breakdown to establish stable screenplay evidence, $screenplay-scene-daoyanzu for prompt-free scene direction, and $screenplay-shot-prose-compiler for the default one-shot-per-paragraph DOCX. Invoke $seedance-shot-prompt-compiler only as an explicit downstream step. Use $dlss5-lighting-director for scoped lighting/material enhancement of an existing image or video prompt.
